page_title: Convoy — a download manager for the Mac

sources.entry: Convoy - Open-source download manager with segmented downloads, browser integration, and HLS and DASH stream support. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/TheDynamicPunk/Convoy) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.name: Convoy
summary.one_liner: Convoy is a free, open-source macOS download manager that splits files into up to 16 segments, takes over downloads from your browser with cookies and logins, and fetches HLS/DASH video streams.
use_cases: Speed up large file downloads on a Mac
Download files that sit behind a website login
Save streaming video (HLS/DASH) to a local file
Resume a download interrupted by quitting the app
Manage a queue of downloads from the menu bar
summary.what_it_does: Convoy splits each file into 1 to 16 segments and downloads them at the same time, falling back to a single stream when a server does not support byte ranges. A browser extension (Chromium-based browsers and Firefox family) hands downloads to the app along with the URL, referrer, cookies and headers, so logged-in downloads work. It can fetch video streams the browser can play, and YouTube via yt-dlp, which the app downloads on request from Settings. Downloads can be paused, resumed across quits, filtered and searched in a queue, and monitored from the menu bar, with notifications on completion and a tool to clear leftovers from interrupted downloads.
notable: Segmented downloads of up to 16 segments per file, with browser cookies and headers passed along
Browser extensions for Chrome, Brave, Edge, Vivaldi, Opera, Arc, Chromium, Firefox, Zen, Floorp, LibreWolf and Waterfox
Fully open source under GPLv3; the download engine is a separate library
Not signed or notarized with an Apple certificate, so first launch requires an Open Anyway step in System Settings
caveats: Not signed with an Apple certificate; macOS blocks first launch and requires manual approval (or xattr command)
No Safari support, as Apple's extension route needs a paid certificate
Not on the Mac App Store; no torrent support, only HTTP and HLS/DASH
